column3: Details
column4: Cultural Notes

column3: Water pipes are ceramic and manufactured in short sections, generally a few feet long, connected by metal fittings.
Material is considered waste only when it can no longer reasonably be repaired, reused, repurposed, composted, remade, or reclaimed.
column4: Solarathi culture emphasizes cycles rather than disposal. Wastefulness is discouraged.

column3: Pottery is repaired while practical. Broken ceramics and stone can become drainage material, construction fill, paving, crushed building material, or mosaics.
column4: Reclaimed mosaic work is a recognizable part of Aldeatus's visual character. Broken objects are viewed as materials rather than automatically as garbage.

column3: Clothing and household textiles are patched, altered, handed down, resized, converted into rags, stuffing, ties, and other useful materials. Only badly exhausted or contaminated fibers reach final disposal/burning.
Farms, ranches, vineyards, and orchards occupy much of the privately owned land surrounding the Great Lake. Aldeatus occupies primarily one side of the lake between the shore and mountains.
column4: The Great Lake region is both an agricultural center and highly desirable land.

column3: Most households buy fresh food every cycle or every other cycle, purchasing quantities they expect to consume or safely store. Fresh meat is generally purchased close to when it will be cooked.
column4: Frequent food shopping is an ordinary part of city life.

column3: Most homes have a small underground or partially underground cold/root-storage area sufficient for ordinary household needs.
column4: Limited household storage contributes to frequent shopping.

column3: Wealthy households may own horses and carriages for longer journeys through Aldeatus or hire private carriage services when needed.
column4: Private carriage ownership provides convenience and status, although wealthy residents still walk shorter distances.

column3: Residents can live considerable distances from their workplaces. Palace, civic, commercial, and other workers may commute between city tiers by public carriage or on foot. Shopkeepers commonly live above or near their businesses, but this is not required of most professions.
column4: Palace workers are largely ordinary Aldeatus residents rather than a separate palace-dwelling population.

column3: Flat roofs, balconies, courtyards, and other household spaces are commonly used to grow herbs and small useful plants.
column4: Urban households commonly produce at least small quantities of useful plants themselves.

column3: Thick walls, pale plaster, courtyards, open windows, shade, airflow, awnings, fabric shades, and usable outdoor spaces help keep homes comfortable during warm weather.
column4: Aldeatus's architecture responds physically to climate rather than relying upon magic.

column3: Exterior shutters close during winter. Removable textile or fur insulation can be fitted against or within them to reduce heat loss.
column4: Installing winter insulation is a normal seasonal household task.

column3: Natural mountain ice is harvested and transported into Aldeatus. Enchanted containers slow melting during transport and storage.
column4: Physical resources and magic are intentionally used together.

column3: Children are expected to make small, age-appropriate contributions to their households and neighborhoods. These may include feeding communal poultry, collecting eggs, helping with gardens, carrying suitable food scraps, assisting with distribution of communal goods, and tending appropriate shared spaces. Older or trained children may assist adults with specialized work such as beekeeping.
column4: Contribution teaches responsibility and belonging rather than being treated primarily as economic labor.

column3: Eggs, honey, and other small products generated through communal neighborhood spaces are distributed among residents, with particular attention given to households currently in need. Children often help collect and distribute these goods as part of their community responsibilities. Surplus can be preserved or distributed more broadly.
column4: Shared neighborhood resources carry an expectation of mutual care rather than strict individual ownership.

column3: Rooftops, balconies, and courtyards commonly contain small hearths or cooking fires used during warm weather so cooking does not unnecessarily heat the home's interior. Water and basic fire-control materials are kept nearby.
column4: Seasonal household routines respond strongly to Aldeatus's climate.

column3: Household water is heated over stoves or fireplaces as needed.
column4: Ordinary households have access to hot water; it simply requires physical work and fuel.

column3: During warm weather, washed textiles are hung across courtyards, balconies, terraces, and rooftops. During winter they are dried indoors near fireplaces and stoves.
column4: Lines of drying clothing are a normal visual feature of Aldeatus's residential neighborhoods.

column3: At approximately 12 Solturns of age, a child chooses a primary profession or trade and begins formal long-term apprenticeship. The choice determines their primary training but does not permanently bind them to that profession. Adults can retrain or change careers later, and broad practical/business skills can transfer to other work.
column4: Choosing a profession establishes a primary training path rather than an irreversible social role.

column3: Exceptionally powerful or unusual children may show identifiable magical signs much earlier. Sorren's magic was recognizable from birth and he was formally tested around age 3–4, which is considered extremely early.
column4: Early manifestation is noteworthy rather than normal.

column3: Starting school teaches basic magical control and safety alongside ordinary academics. Because usable magic most commonly manifests between approximately ages 6–10, children are taught according to their current stage of development. Children whose magic has not yet manifested learn recognition and safety principles until practical instruction becomes applicable.
column4: Controlling one's ability is treated as foundational education.

column3: Children commonly consider their magical abilities when exploring professions because working with one's natural abilities makes certain tasks substantially easier. However, there is no requirement that someone's profession correspond to their magic.
column4: Magic influences occupation without functioning as a caste system.

column3: Children commonly consider their magical abilities when exploring professions because working with one's natural abilities makes certain tasks substantially easier. However, there is no requirement that someone's profession correspond to their magic.
column4: Magic influences occupation without functioning as a caste system. A person's power may make a profession easier without defining what they are permitted to become.

column3: Midwives monitor maternal health, progression of pregnancy, fetal growth, positioning, movement, heartbeat when it can be assessed, and signs of complications.
column4: Centuries of magical observation have contributed to strong knowledge of pregnancy and fetal development even among nonmagical practitioners.

column3: Infants are primarily cared for by their parents. Extended family and close friends commonly help so parents can sleep, recover, work, or simply have a break.
column4: Parents are considered the primary caregivers without being expected to provide every hour of care without assistance.

column3: Grandparents and other close relatives or friends may come to the home to settle the baby, prepare food, hold the infant, help with household work, or allow the parents to rest.
column4: Infant care exists within a wider family and community network while parents remain the primary caregivers.

column3: Young children commonly sleep with their parents during infancy and early toddlerhood. Families transition them to their own sleeping space at roughly ages 1–3 depending on the child's sleep, available space, and what works for the household.
column4: There is no culturally fixed age at which a small child must sleep separately.

column3: The amount of fire and heat being manipulated matters. A skilled wielder can extinguish or control a relatively small fire, but a major structure fire produces too much flame and heat for one person to simply extinguish magically.
column4: Powerful magic reduces difficulty but does not eliminate physical scale, logistics, or danger.

column3: Solarathi justice generally favors restitution, compulsory service, rehabilitation, and protection of the community over long-term imprisonment. Punishment should require the offender to confront or repair the harm they caused where reasonably possible.
column4: Simply confining someone for years is viewed as accomplishing little for either the harmed person or the wider community. Justice focuses on repair where possible and protection where repair is insufficient.

column3: Someone hired for a single cycle or similarly short period is normally paid when that work is completed.
column4: Payment timing follows the scale and duration of the agreement rather than a universal payroll system.

column3: Residential neighborhoods commonly center around shared greens, courtyards, parks, or small squares where paths converge. These spaces can contain gardens, poultry, beehives, fire-water basins, gathering areas, and nearby everyday markets.
column4: These spaces are functional centers of neighborhood life rather than purely decorative parks. Neighborhood communal spaces fall within the area's local administration while residents participate in everyday use and upkeep.

column3: Most residential areas are primarily pedestrian. Smaller streets, alleys, stairs, and walking paths connect homes with neighborhood centers and major roads. Stairs often provide more direct movement between Aldeatus's tiers while carriage roads take longer, gentler routes.
column4: Walking is the normal means of short-distance travel.

column3: Salting, drying, pickling, cheesemaking, fermentation, and wine production/storage are established preservation methods. Households keep preserved foods alongside frequently purchased fresh goods.
column4: Food preservation is ordinary household knowledge.

column3: Much of Aldeatus's ordinary food comes from agricultural properties surrounding the Great Lake. Producers move goods into the city by road, cart, or lake depending upon location and convenience.
column4: Local production keeps fresh food closely connected to the surrounding countryside.

column3: Planned surgery is performed within temple clinics, where sanitation, trained staff, Keepers, supplies, and specialized magic are available. Surgery outside a temple occurs only when an emergency makes transport impossible or more dangerous.
column4: The temple is considered the safest recognized environment for invasive treatment.

column3: Men and women can own property, operate businesses, earn money, train in professions, employ others, inherit economic responsibilities, and control finances under the same basic rules.
column4: Profession and economic role are shaped more by aptitude, magic, interest, training, household circumstances, and opportunity than by sex.

column3: Businesses normally close around midday for the main meal and rest period before reopening afterward when appropriate.
column4: Midday closure is a normal part of Aldeatus's rhythm and allows work schedules to accommodate meals, family, rest, and the warmer portion of the cycle.

column3: Communal greens commonly maintain beehives alongside poultry and gardens. Bees support neighborhood vegetation and provide honey and wax. Trained residents or appointed caretakers maintain communal hives, with older or trained children able to assist.
column4: Bees are valued for both their products and their role in sustaining plant life.

column3: Public bathhouses are common and used across social classes. Private household baths also exist. Baths are inset into the floor/ground and have drains. Public baths are often more convenient because large quantities of heated water are maintained there. Laundry facilities may also accompany bathhouses.
column4: Public bathing is hygienic and social rather than a marker of poverty.

column3: State-supported guilds provide another route for apprenticeship and professional training. They coexist with private masters rather than monopolizing professions.
column4: Guilds give the government a way to preserve important skills and expand access without eliminating independent craftspeople.

column3: A person who is never formally tested still possesses their magic and may eventually unlock or develop it independently, but doing so is more difficult.
column4: Testing provides guidance and a safer/easier transition into magical use.

column3: Solarath uses physical coinage as its primary currency.
column4: Coins provide a broadly understood exchange system, while direct barter or trade can still occur when convenient.

column3: Neighborhoods have covered stone or clay refuse containers. Large estates may maintain private collection points. Civic sanitation workers collect materials and transport them to appropriate reuse, treatment, or disposal facilities.
column4: Sanitation work is respected as necessary civic labor.

column3: Shared poultry enclosures are common around neighborhood greens/community spaces. Birds provide eggs and meat while consuming appropriate food scraps. Children may help feed birds and collect eggs as part of neighborhood responsibilities.
column4: Eggs can be distributed within the neighborhood, with some going toward residents in greater need. Poultry contributes simultaneously to food supply, community support, and waste reduction.

column3: Most Solarathi homes contain at least one stained-glass element, including relatively ordinary households.
column4: Stained glass is part of ordinary Solarathi visual culture rather than being restricted to temples and palaces. Veshalor is especially renowned for the craft.

column3: The Great Lake is one of Aldeatus's major transportation routes. Farms, estates, settlements, and other properties around the lake can move people and goods to the capital by boat rather than traveling around the shoreline.
column4: Waterfront access has substantial practical as well as aesthetic value.

column3: Many homes contain a central open courtyard providing daylight, airflow, outdoor living space, and passive cooling.
column4: Courtyards are everyday domestic spaces rather than purely decorative features.

column3: Household cooking primarily uses fireplaces and stoves, often the same structures that contribute to household heating.
Flat, usable roofs are common and serve as additional household space for growing plants, sitting, working, drying laundry, and sometimes cooking.
column4: Roofs effectively expand usable living space in dense neighborhoods.

column3: Home is the default location for treatment. A physician or midwife determines when a condition exceeds what can safely be managed there and temple care becomes necessary.
column4: Medical care operates as a progression from household care to professional home care to temple treatment rather than beginning at a hospital for every illness.

column3: Bed-sharing with an infant under approximately one year is practiced specifically when the infant has a breastfeeding parent sharing the bed. Generations of observation have led people to recognize that breastfeeding parents sleep and wake differently and remain more responsive to the infant during sleep.
column4: This is practical knowledge developed through generations of observation rather than requiring a modern physiological explanation.

column3: Ash produced through controlled burning is collected and sorted where practical for appropriate secondary uses in agriculture, manufacturing, construction, or other processes.
column4: Even the remains of burned materials should be useful when safely possible.

column3: Usable magic most commonly begins appearing between approximately ages 6–10. A child usually first describes an unfamiliar sensation growing beneath or within the skin, followed by small accidental manifestations that parents or caregivers begin noticing.
column4: Families generally recognize the signs and bring the child to a temple once manifestation begins.

column3: Children attend starting school from approximately 5–9 Solturns of age. Schools teach reading, writing, basic arithmetic, foundational knowledge, and basic magical control and safety as children's abilities begin to emerge.
column4: Foundational literacy, numeracy, and safe control of one's eventual magic are considered education every child should receive.

column3: Nobles and officials working from the palace operate the central government beneath the Crown. They receive matters from regional and local nobles, coordinate resources between areas, administer central offices and Royal Court functions, and manage kingdom-wide concerns.
column4: The palace is a working governmental complex as well as a royal residence.

column3: Nobles and officials working from the palace operate the central government beneath the Crown. They receive matters from regional and local nobles, coordinate resources between areas, administer central offices and Royal Court functions, and manage kingdom-wide concerns.
column4: The palace is a working governmental complex as well as the royal residence.

column3: Broken or unwanted metal is returned to metalworkers for reuse/remelting. Glass is reclaimed and remelted where practical rather than burned or discarded.
column4: Skilled/material-intensive resources remain valuable after the original object fails.

column3: Possessing solar power creates a strong expectation of rulership but does not make someone automatically entitled to govern regardless of their conduct or ability to perform the role. If the solar holder becomes unable or unsuitable to rule, another member of the royal family can become monarch.
column4: This distinction allows Solarath to respond to an unfit solar ruler without requiring society to deny the religious meaning it assigns to their power.

column3: Smaller courtyards can be temporarily covered with fitted panels during winter. Larger courtyards are more likely to use heavy curtains, screens, or protected sections rather than completely enclosing the entire space.
column4: The function and appearance of the same household space changes substantially throughout the Solturn.

column3: Small infant beds are commonly kept immediately beside the parents' bed and are used when bed-sharing is not appropriate or desired.
column4: Keeping a young infant physically close to the parents at night is normal even when the infant is not sharing their bed.

column3: As household wealth increases, homes generally become larger and more separated, with more rooms, larger courtyards, gardens, terraces, and eventually private carriage houses/stables.
Checking that manually supplied neighborhood fire basins remain full is one of the communal responsibilities older children can perform.
column4: The task gives children a meaningful role in protecting their community without expecting them to fight fires.

column3: When labor begins, a family member, friend, or neighbor fetches the midwife. Birth normally occurs at home unless complications require temple care.
column4: Birth commonly draws upon the household and trusted community for practical support while the midwife retains the professional medical role.

column3: Members of the royal family often possess substantial privilege, wealth, access, and social status because of their relationship to the ruling household. Royal blood alone does not make their Heart Flames inherently more valuable.
column4: Royal privilege is understood as a consequence of family and political position rather than evidence that the entire royal bloodline consists of spiritually superior people.

column3: People who cannot reasonably support themselves because of age, disability, or similar lasting circumstances can receive state support.
column4: Solarathi society distinguishes inability to work from unwillingness to contribute when capable. Long-term support is understood as a communal obligation toward people whose circumstances prevent ordinary self-support.

column3: Temples contain clinics that function as Aldeatus's hospitals. Patients requiring intensive treatment, prolonged observation, specialized procedures, surgery, or magical care can be taken there.
column4: Temples care for the body as well as the Heart Flame, connecting medicine with Solarathi beliefs surrounding life, suffering, and death.

column3: Sexual and child-related offenses have distinct judicial-band patterns that are immediately distinguishable from ordinary restitution and service sentences.
column4: The distinctive pattern allows caregivers and community members to recognize restrictions relevant to safety without requiring all sentenced people to be treated as though they committed the same kind of offense.

column3: Collection, sewer maintenance, waste treatment, controlled burning, and related sanitation work are recognized civic professions. Workers may be employed through local administration, Crown-funded civic services, or contracted organizations.
column4: Work that sustains the community is respected for the function it provides.

column3: Small permanent shops and markets are distributed throughout Aldeatus, with many shopkeepers living above their businesses. Businesses establish schedules according to trade and demand, and some operate into the night.
column4: Shopping is part of ordinary neighborhood life. Businesses normally close for the midday meal regardless of their broader operating schedule.

column3: Sexual violence against children automatically bypasses ordinary final sentencing authority and becomes a Royal Court matter.
column4: Children are considered particularly deserving of protection because adults hold substantially greater physical, social, and practical power over them.

column3: Execution is exceptionally rare and reserved for the most extreme cases, particularly mass killing or severe repeated violence when the Royal Court determines that neither reintegration nor another protective sentence can adequately protect others.
column4: Execution remains exceptional because deliberately extinguishing a living person's Heart Flame is itself regarded as an extraordinary act. Solarathi justice rejects the idea that simply taking “a flame for a flame” automatically creates justice.

column3: Fire magic broadly allows interaction with flame and heat. Like other powers, individual wielders have different specialties and strengths rather than identical abilities.
column4: A broad magical classification describes what someone can interact with, not an identical set of abilities every wielder possesses.

column3: Every mortal—person, beast, or bloom—bears a Heart Flame, a living fragment of the Eternal Flame. Humans and other humanoid peoples alone manifest specialized usable magic beyond the life-sustaining Heart Flame. Animals and plants possess Heart Flames but do not wield specialized magic.
column4: Life itself is sacred because every mortal carries a fragment of the Eternal Flame.

column3: A secure dungeon exists beneath the outer portion of the palace complex, potentially carved partly into the mountain or stone beneath the Royal Court and guard areas. It primarily holds prisoners whose cases fall under royal authority or who require exceptional security.
column4: The dungeon is associated with royal justice and exceptional security rather than ordinary petty crime.

column3: Horse stables exist within Aldeatus near carriage houses, transportation hubs, and major roads. Public carriage systems maintain access to substantial stabling, while wealthy estates may have private carriage houses and stables.
column4: Horses are a normal part of city life despite most large livestock remaining outside dense neighborhoods.

column3: The palace court represents kingdom-level government in matters requiring central authority. It participates in noble appointments and removals, receives escalated governmental issues, and supports the Crown in kingdom-wide administration and Royal Court matters.
column4: It acts as the kingdom-level counterpart to local councils and noble administrations.

column3: Safe leftovers are retained for later consumption. Appropriate scraps are given to communal poultry or other animals, while suitable plant material can be composted. Unsafe material enters the appropriate waste stream.
column4: Food reuse reflects the wider Solarathi expectation that resources should be used as fully as reasonably possible.

column3: People actively serving court-ordered labor or service wear broad standardized judicial bands. Woven geometric patterns identify broad offense categories, while bright flame-like colors indicate an active sentence. The band remains visible on the outermost layer of clothing.
column4: The band distinguishes compulsory criminal service from ordinary paid civic work while allowing sentenced people to otherwise retain ordinary clothing and personal identity.

column3: Permanent bodily intervention is an accepted sentence for sexual violence against children and may also be imposed for repeated or exceptionally severe sexual violence against adults.
column4: The punishment is understood as both a severe consequence and an attempt to restrict the offender's ability to repeat particular forms of harm.

column3: Aldeatus occupies primarily one side of the Great Lake between the shoreline and mountains. The city rises toward the mountains in visible tiers. Broad carriage roads curve and climb between levels while narrower pedestrian streets, alleys, and stairways provide more direct routes. Neighborhoods commonly form around shared greens/courtyards and local services.
column4: The city's elevation strongly shapes transportation, drainage, architecture, water distribution, and its recognizable layered appearance from across the lake.

column3: The monarch is the highest level of Solarathi government. The Crown handles kingdom-wide policy, major disputes, Royal Court matters, large-scale allocation of resources, and international affairs.
column4: Solarath is a monarchy, but the Crown is not expected to personally administer every settlement or ordinary dispute.

column3: A child's Avelum and Solaver are sworn Radiant Guardians who form part of the child's trusted lifelong support network. Parents remain primary caregivers, followed by the child's wider family and support network; Radiant Guardians can provide guidance, care, protection, and relief for the parents when needed.
column4: The oath carries genuine lifelong responsibility toward the child rather than being merely ceremonial. Guardians supplement rather than replace ordinary family relationships.

column3: Pregnant people receive regular midwife visits throughout pregnancy. Early in pregnancy they normally travel to the midwife; as pregnancy progresses and travel becomes more difficult, the midwife begins making home visits.
column4: Pregnancy is routinely monitored rather than receiving professional attention only when something goes wrong.

column3: A noble title normally passes to the holder's oldest child and then through that child's descendants. Sex does not affect succession. This is the expected path rather than an absolute right; an heir considered unsuitable can be passed over for another appropriate successor.
column4: Political office and inherent worth remain distinct. Passing over an heir means they are considered unsuitable for that responsibility, not that their Heart Flame is lesser.

column3: Skilled fire-wielders may assist in controlling existing fires by manipulating manageable portions of flame or heat. They can help contain sections, redirect flame, reduce heat, extinguish smaller fires, or prevent spread depending upon their specialty.
column4: Fire-wielders are useful because they can interact directly with the hazard, not because fire magic automatically defeats every fire.

column3: Apprentices learn both their profession and the supporting skills required to practice it independently. Training can include tools, materials, sourcing, customers, pricing, trade, recordkeeping, and other relevant business knowledge. Apprenticeships may be undertaken through individual masters or state-run guilds.
column4: A trained craftsperson is expected to understand both the work itself and how to function economically within the profession.

column3: Apprentices learn the profession itself plus the supporting skills necessary to practice it independently. Training includes practical work, materials, tools, sourcing, selling, customers, pricing, trade, recordkeeping, and other relevant business knowledge.
column4: A trained craftsperson is expected to understand both the work itself and how to function economically within the profession.

column3: True Temple Keepers must possess magic related to the body. Their abilities allow them to perform the Keeper's established roles surrounding life and death as well as caring for patients within temple clinics.
column4: Keepers occupy an unusual position between religious service and medicine. Their magical eligibility does not eliminate the need for extensive medical and religious training.

column3: Cold-producing abilities exist and may represent a branch or specialty of water-related magic. Cold magic can be infused into suitable reservoirs and used to maintain low temperatures.
column4: Magic supplements ordinary technology and resource use rather than making them obsolete.

column3: Children are raised with deep respect for the Heart Flame present in every living being. Deliberately ending another person's life is therefore both a legal crime and a profound moral and religious violation.
column4: Respect for another person's Heart Flame contributes to murder being comparatively uncommon without eliminating violence or crime.

column3: A person who manifests solar power is believed to carry a larger portion of the Eternal Flame than an ordinary mortal. The solar abilities themselves are understood as evidence and manifestation of that greater portion.
column4: Solarathi theology genuinely regards the solar Heart Flame as unusually sacred and inherently elevated. This creates a deliberate exception within an otherwise strongly egalitarian theology of mortal worth.

column3: Dedicated sewer channels carry wastewater downhill and away from populated areas toward treatment facilities. Sewage is kept separate from the Great Lake and drinking-water infrastructure.
column4: Polluting the Great Lake or drinking supply is understood to be dangerous and unclean.

column3: Aldeatus receives water through gravity-fed infrastructure. Water travels downhill through ceramic pipes into cisterns, public fountains, bathhouses, homes, and other distribution points.
column4: Gravity is the default; magic supplements the physical system rather than replacing it.

column3: The solar-power holder is normally expected to be Solarath's primary ruler because the power is interpreted as divine evidence of an exceptional connection to the Eternal Flame. Solar inheritance is not sex-based; women and men can manifest the power and rule.
column4: Solarath expects the solar holder to rule under ordinary circumstances, but recognizes that divine or spiritual significance and governmental competence are not identical qualities.

column3: Taxes are collected primarily through businesses rather than ordinary workers being individually taxed on every wage payment. Tax is based upon the business's usable surplus rather than simply gross revenue.
column4: The system treats money required to keep a business functioning as different from disposable profit.

column3: New serious offenses committed while under post-sentence identification are treated especially seriously because the offender has already undergone sentencing, supervised service, counseling, and opportunities for rehabilitation.
column4: Repeated offending changes the justice system's focus from restoration toward long-term protection of the community.

column3: Nobles serve as administrators responsible for districts, towns, groups of settlements, regions, or other governmental responsibilities. Titles carry authority and social status but are fundamentally associated with administrative duties rather than proof of greater inherent worth.
column4: Nobility creates hierarchy of authority and responsibility without creating a corresponding hierarchy of ordinary spiritual worth.

column3: Nobles serve as administrators responsible for particular districts, towns, groups of settlements, regions, or governmental responsibilities.
column4: Nobility is understood as a governmental role as well as a social class. Solarathi theology does not make ordinary nobles spiritually superior to the people they govern.

column3: Noble titles can be acquired through several routes, including royal lineage, finances or wealth, significant service or acts, and other forms of Crown recognition or appointment. Nobility is not exclusively hereditary, and possessing a title carries governmental and social responsibilities.
column4: Solarathi nobility is intended to justify status partly through responsibility and service rather than lineage alone.

column3: Noble titles correspond primarily to the size or scope of the territory or responsibility administered rather than simply personal prestige or wealth. Titles can be inherited, newly granted, transferred, declined, or removed. New titles may be granted through royal lineage, resources, significant service, demonstrated ability, or other forms of governmental recognition.
column4: Nobility is not a permanently closed hereditary class. Rank represents governmental responsibility as well as social status.

column3: Animals are raised, hunted, and killed for food and useful materials. Meat, fat, hide, fur, bone, horn, antler, sinew, and other practical remains are used whenever possible.
column4: Killing animals is accepted as part of the natural cycle. The animal's Heart Flame is thanked for its sacrifice in sustaining other life, and wasting useful remains is considered disrespectful.

column3: Sewage is carried outside the dense city to treatment areas. Solids and liquids can be separated, treated, and potentially reused, with suitable solids contributing to agriculture and treated water potentially used for irrigation/wetland systems.
column4: Human waste is another material that can potentially be made useful rather than something that simply disappears.

column3: Gaining or removing a noble title requires participation from both the relevant local council and palace-level government rather than unilateral action by either the Crown or a local faction. Statements from people directly affected by the administration can be considered when a noble's fitness is reviewed.
column4: Noble authority is expected to remain accountable both upward to the kingdom and downward to the people being governed.

column3: Homes are deliberately insulated against both summer heat and winter cold. Passive construction is more important than magical temperature control.
column4: Seasonal adaptation is built into ordinary architecture.

column3: People serving lengthy compulsory labor or service sentences can live in supervised communal residences resembling simple apartments or dormitories rather than prison cells. Food, clothing, shelter, and basic necessities are provided because they cannot earn ordinary wages while serving the sentence.
column4: Offenders remain part of productive society while under restriction and supervision rather than being entirely removed from ordinary life.

column3: The palace dungeon is separated from the royal family's private living areas by guarded passages, court and administrative spaces, barracks, and other secured portions of the palace.
column4: The palace is simultaneously a residence and governmental complex, so spaces associated with punishment and security are deliberately removed from ordinary royal domestic life.

column3: Aldeatus operates shared passenger carriages along major roads, functioning as public transportation between major areas and elevations of the city.
column4: Particularly useful in a city whose tiered geography makes some journeys physically demanding.

column3: Solarathi society distinguishes authority, ability, wealth, responsibility, and inherent worth. With the major theological exception of actual solar-power holders, humanoid Heart Flames are considered fundamentally equal in inherent worth. Wealth, profession, sex, family, ordinary magical ability, royal relationship, and noble title do not make one ordinary person's Heart Flame more valuable than another's.
column4: This distinction allows Solarath to maintain substantial social and political hierarchy without teaching that ordinary lower-ranked people are lesser beings.

column3: Unlawful killing can result in substantial compulsory service or stronger protective sentences rather than automatic execution. Self-defense, defense of another, accident, negligence, and deliberate murder are legally distinguished.
column4: Taking another person's Heart Flame is considered extraordinarily serious, but deliberately extinguishing the offender's Heart Flame is not regarded as inherently restorative or equivalent justice.

column3: Problems are handled at the smallest level capable of addressing them. Local matters stay local; problems exceeding local resources move to the responsible noble and then to central palace government when necessary.
column4: Authority is decentralized for ordinary administration while retaining a clear route to higher government when local resources or authority are insufficient.

column3: Problems are handled at the smallest level capable of addressing them. Local matters stay local; problems exceeding local authority or resources move to the responsible noble and then to central palace government when necessary.
column4: Solarathi government is decentralized for ordinary administration while maintaining a route to higher authority when local systems are insufficient.

column3: Formal apprenticeship generally lasts approximately eight Solturns, from around age 12 until age 20. Apprentices move progressively from observation and basic tasks to skilled supervised work. Training may occur under an individual master or through a state-run guild.
column4: Competence is expected to come from years of supervised practical experience rather than a short period of schooling.

column3: Buildings requiring water above the natural gravity-fed level collect it in a lower basin/cistern and move it upward through pipes. Enchanted junctions are spaced periodically rather than enchanting the entire pipe.
column4: Water flowing upward is an understated sign of wealth: ordinary infrastructure follows gravity; money can overcome it.

column3: The midwife continues visiting mother and infant for approximately six weeks after birth. Visits monitor postpartum healing, feeding, infant growth and health, and other concerns.
column4: Birth does not mark the end of professional maternal care. Recovery and the infant's transition into life are treated as an extended period requiring attention.

column3: Major roads have dedicated streetlights. Smaller pedestrian neighborhoods rely more heavily on doorway lights and lighting maintained around communal spaces.
column4: Lighting follows the city's hierarchy of movement: major routes receive dedicated infrastructure while neighborhoods collectively provide much of their own illumination.

column3: Some body-related magic specializes in sensing rather than altering the body. These individuals may perceive heartbeats, blood flow, internal movement, organ activity, fetal movement, and other bodily processes that cannot normally be directly observed.
column4: Generations of sensing practitioners have substantially expanded Avelian understanding of living anatomy.

column3: Small fires are handled immediately by occupants. Larger fires trigger a neighborhood response using nearby water supplies while someone summons professional assistance.
column4: Neighbors are expected to help protect one another's homes because dense urban fire threatens more than the household where it began.

column3: Magical powers belong to broader forms or types, but individuals commonly have narrower areas in which their magic works most naturally or strongly. They can still perform some more general applications within their broader ability.
column4: A person's specialty influences what comes easily without absolutely determining what they can do.

column3: Beginning around 10 Solturns of age, children start exploring professions and apprenticeship paths. From approximately 10–12 they may try several forms of work before committing to a primary profession.
column4: Children are expected to experience different forms of work before choosing their long-term training.

column3: Around six Solturns into formal training—approximately age 18—an apprentice begins performing substantial professional work under supervision. They are capable of meaningful professional labor but are not yet considered fully trained.
column4: Being capable of doing the work is distinct from being recognized as fully trained.

column3: Property crimes generally require repayment or replacement of what was taken or damaged.
column4: The goal is to restore what was taken rather than punish theft through unrelated suffering.

column3: Jointly owned property is divided equally when a couple divorces. Property that remained individually owned generally remains with its owner unless it had previously been made shared.
column4: Marriage does not automatically erase individual economic identity, even though couples may choose to combine most or all property during the marriage.

column3: Married couples decide for themselves how to organize money and property according to what works for their household. Finances may be combined, partially combined, or managed separately.
column4: Flame Binding does not erase the economic independence of either spouse or impose one legally required household-finance arrangement.

column3: Parents retain equal parental standing and responsibility after separation. There is no automatic preference for the mother or father. Courts can alter arrangements where safety, abandonment, inability to provide care, or other serious circumstances require it.
column4: Solarathi family law treats parenthood as a responsibility belonging equally to mothers and fathers rather than assuming children naturally belong to one sex after separation.

column3: Large shipments move from docks along major roads by cart or wagon to warehouses, markets, merchants, palace suppliers, and institutional buyers. Smaller quantities are then distributed into pedestrian neighborhoods.

Avelian medicine has a deep understanding of anatomy despite relatively simple pharmaceuticals. Generations of body-sensing magic have allowed practitioners to study living anatomy, circulation, pregnancy, organ function, injury, and other internal processes.
column4: Magical discoveries become ordinary medical knowledge rather than remaining exclusive knowledge of magic users.

column3: Neighborhoods are the first layer of social stability. Communities try to ensure people have food and other necessities when they temporarily cannot provide for themselves, reducing crimes driven by desperation.
column4: Preventing a neighbor from becoming desperate is considered part of maintaining a healthy community. Community support is therefore understood partly as crime prevention as well as mutual care.

column3: Most illness and minor injury are treated within the home. Family members provide basic care, and medical professionals can be called or visited when needed.
column4: Being cared for at home is the ordinary expectation rather than a sign of inadequate care. Families and neighbors are expected to help one another during ordinary illness.

column3: Because apprenticeships teach broad practical and commercial skills, completing or partially completing one profession gives a person knowledge useful in other careers.
column4: Career changes are considered practical and prior training is not regarded as wasted simply because someone changes professions.

column3: A child may apprentice directly under an individual craftsperson or professional, learning within the actual workplace.
column4: Knowledge can be transmitted directly from practitioner to apprentice, allowing professional traditions and individual techniques to continue across generations.

column3: Taxes, trade tariffs, and Crown contributions fund communal infrastructure such as roads, fountains, baths, sanitation, fire response, starting schools, public spaces, and other state services.
column4: Royal wealth is expected to contribute toward maintaining the kingdom and capital rather than functioning solely as the monarch's private household wealth.

column3: Most formally prosecuted crimes are brought before a public court. Evidence and accusations are heard and a legal judgment is made publicly.
column4: Visible proceedings support the idea that justice is accountable to the community rather than occurring entirely behind palace walls.

column3: Dangerous offenders who cannot safely return to ordinary society may be relocated to isolated, controlled areas within Solarathi territory rather than simply expelled across the kingdom's border.
column4: Solarath does not consider knowingly transferring a dangerous offender into an innocent neighboring population an acceptable solution. Restricted exile preserves the offender's life while removing ordinary freedom of residence.

column3: The royal palace maintains direct relationships with farms, ranches, vineyards, merchants, and other suppliers to provide reliable everyday provisions while still participating in the broader Aldeatus economy.

Jails and dungeons primarily hold accused people awaiting judgment, people awaiting transfer or sentencing, or dangerous individuals who cannot currently be allowed into the community. Long prison sentences are unusual.
column4: Confinement is primarily a security measure rather than Solarath's standard form of punishment.

column3: Aldeatus's nobles meet as a council to discuss conditions within their respective areas, coordinate city-wide needs, and redistribute resources when necessary.
column4: The council allows information and resources to move across Aldeatus while decisions affecting only one district remain local.

column3: Aldeatus's nobles meet as a council to discuss conditions within their respective areas, coordinate city-wide needs, and redistribute resources where necessary.
column4: The council allows information and resources to move across Aldeatus while matters affecting only one district remain local.

column3: Midwives provide pregnancy, labor, birth, postpartum, and related reproductive care. When labor begins, someone from the household or neighborhood normally fetches the family's chosen or nearest available midwife.
column4: Birth and reproductive care are recognized professional specialties rather than being treated solely as informal women's household knowledge.

column3: Not everyone who works within a temple is a Keeper. Temples require people performing religious, administrative, domestic, medical-support, maintenance, educational, and other duties.
column4: Working in a temple and being a Temple Keeper are distinct roles. Religious service is not restricted to those possessing body-related magic.

column3: People awaiting ordinary hearings or serving very short periods of confinement can be held in secure city facilities near courts or guard stations rather than inside the palace.
column4: Routine detention remains decentralized rather than making every accused person a royal prisoner.

column3: Aldeatus is divided among several noble administrations. Each oversees the needs, tax resources, infrastructure, and public services of its portion of the city while coordinating matters that affect Aldeatus as a whole.
column4: Administrative boundaries organize services without making each district economically self-contained.

column3: Aldeatus is divided among several noble administrations. Each oversees the needs, tax resources, infrastructure, and public services of its portion of the city while coordinating matters affecting Aldeatus as a whole.
column4: Administrative boundaries organize services without making each district economically independent from the rest of Aldeatus.

column3: Candles are the ordinary source of household lighting after dark. Homes commonly maintain a light near their entrance.
column4: Doorway lights make pedestrian neighborhoods safer and more welcoming after dark.

column3: Beeswax from neighborhood and agricultural hives contributes to candle production. Candles are a major source of household nighttime lighting.
column4: Beekeeping supports both food production and household lighting.

column3: Even families that normally bed-share may move the infant to a bedside bed when circumstances make sharing inappropriate, such as when a parent is ill, impaired, or otherwise unable to sleep responsively.
column4: Midwives and parents recognize that an ordinarily accepted sleeping arrangement can become inappropriate when circumstances change.

column3: Chickens and other useful poultry can be kept within Aldeatus, especially in communal neighborhood spaces and private courtyards with sufficient room.
column4: Poultry contributes food while consuming suitable household scraps.

column3: Physicians diagnose and treat illness and injury and can make house calls. When someone becomes ill, a family member, neighbor, or other household member commonly goes to fetch a physician.
column4: Most patients remain at home unless their condition requires temple care. Physicians therefore work substantially within homes rather than only from dedicated medical buildings.

column3: Water-wielders are especially useful during major fires because they can rapidly manipulate water stored in basins or supplied by fountains and cisterns. Most cannot create water and therefore depend upon existing supplies.
column4: Fire infrastructure is intentionally designed so responders do not have to depend upon the chance presence of someone capable of creating water.

column3: Fireplaces and stoves provide household heat during winter and often double as cooking heat.

Aldeatus has a Greek/Mediterranean-influenced architectural style. Buildings are commonly plastered, closely built, bright, and designed around shade, airflow, seasonal temperature control, and usable outdoor space.

Outside Aldeatus, most Great Lake shoreline is privately owned. Working farms/ranches and other agricultural properties dominate much of it, with wealthy private estates occupying some desirable areas.
The Great Lake connects through a river system toward the sea. Foreign and coastal goods can travel inland through river ports and eventually reach Aldeatus.
column4: Aldeatus's waterways make the inland capital an important trade center.

column3: Major routes are broad enough for carriages and carts to travel in both directions while leaving space for pedestrians. They connect major districts, markets, civic areas, entrances, docks, and the routes climbing between city tiers.
column4: Major roads are transportation corridors rather than the default form of residential streets.

column3: Some buildings use sloped roofs, particularly three-story homes where the upper floor occupies only part of the footprint and the remaining space forms a terrace or balcony.

Apothecary shops prepare and sell medicines. Residents can purchase ordinary remedies such as pain medicine directly, while physicians and midwives obtain or direct patients toward more specialized preparations.
column4: Apothecaries form a normal part of neighborhood commerce and bridge household treatment with professional medicine.

column3: Horses, carts, wagons, and carriages primarily use Aldeatus's broader roads. They are uncommon within narrow pedestrian neighborhoods except where access has specifically been designed for them.
column4: Large parts of the city remain substantially pedestrian despite regular horse traffic on major routes.

column3: Cattle, sheep, goats, and other large agricultural livestock generally remain on farms or outskirts rather than within dense Aldeatus. Horses are the major exception because they are necessary for urban transportation and therefore have dedicated city stables.
column4: Limiting large livestock reduces crowding and waste within pedestrian neighborhoods.

column3: Household work is performed by whoever is available rather than being inherently assigned to one gender. Children and adults who are already home often perform more routine tasks. If all adults work outside the home, domestic responsibilities are divided as evenly and practically as possible.
column4: Domestic work is treated as necessary household contribution.

column3: Regional nobles communicate unusual needs to Aldeatus. Drought, crop failure, major fire, disease outbreak, infrastructure failure, or similar crises can prompt a request for additional money, food, labor, medical support, or other resources from central government.
column4: A designated administrator represents affected communities rather than requiring individual villages to separately plead their cases before the palace.

column3: Regional nobles communicate unusual needs to Aldeatus. Drought, crop failure, major fire, disease outbreak, infrastructure failure, or similar crises can prompt requests for additional money, food, labor, medical support, magical specialists, or other resources from central government.
column4: A designated administrator represents affected communities rather than requiring individual villages to separately petition the palace.

column3: Public bathhouses commonly include dedicated laundry rooms supplied with abundant water, making them convenient places to wash household textiles. Laundry is carried home wet or damp afterward.
column4: Laundry contributes to bathhouses functioning as regular neighborhood social spaces.

column3: Most medicines are plant-, mineral-, or otherwise naturally derived preparations. Treatments include relatively basic remedies for pain, fever, inflammation, digestive problems, wounds, sleep, and other common conditions.
column4: Household medicinal knowledge overlaps with professional medicine, but serious conditions are still taken to trained practitioners.

column3: Uncomplicated labor and birth normally take place at home under a midwife's care, supported by family, friends, or neighbors as appropriate.
column4: Home birth is the ordinary Solarathi model rather than an alternative to institutional birth.

column3: Body magic can assist healing, diagnosis, stabilization, and other bodily processes, but it does not make the body infinitely repairable. Keepers work with the patient's existing body and Heart Flame rather than simply reversing every injury, illness, disability, or death.
column4: The existence of medical magic does not eliminate illness, disability, pregnancy complications, severe injury, or death. Medical knowledge remains as important as magical power.

column3: Midwives help manage ordinary pregnancy problems such as nausea, pain, fatigue, difficulty eating, and other discomforts using practical care and available medicines.
column4: Pregnancy discomfort is considered worthy of care even when it is not dangerous.

column3: Stone water basins dedicated exclusively to firefighting are positioned throughout neighborhoods, courtyards, markets, and other communal areas. Some are continuously or slowly replenished through gravity-fed water lines; others require manual filling.
column4: Fire water is reserved for emergencies and using it casually is socially unacceptable because doing so could endanger the neighborhood.

column3: Aldeatus maintains trained professional fire responders using conventional firefighting equipment alongside responders who may possess useful magical abilities.
column4: Fire response is considered valuable civic labor, and magical talent alone does not make someone a trained firefighter.

column3: Food merchants, warehouses, mills, and major suppliers maintain much larger storage facilities than households. Grain and other stable foods are stored in bulk.

Once a child's magic begins manifesting, they are brought to a temple for the established testing ceremony. The ceremony identifies or recognizes the nature of the child's magic and helps fully unlock their access to it.
column4: Magical identification has a religious and ceremonial component rather than being purely practical.

column3: Repeated serious offending produces escalating consequences. Someone who commits a grave offense, completes a sentence, and repeatedly commits comparable offenses demonstrates that previous attempts at restitution and rehabilitation have not adequately protected the community.
column4: The justice system allows opportunities for rehabilitation but does not require communities to accept unlimited repeated danger.

column3: Assault and other offenses that cannot be repaired through direct financial restitution can result in compulsory public or community service. More serious offenses require longer or more restrictive service.
column4: The offender is required to contribute back to the society they harmed.

column3: A suitable drawer, box, basket, or similar small contained space can be prepared as an infant bed when necessary rather than every household needing specialized furniture.
column4: Practicality and keeping the infant safely nearby matter more than possessing specialized baby furniture.

column3: Two- and three-story homes are common. Many are townhouse-like structures sharing walls with neighboring buildings.
column4: Dense construction keeps residential neighborhoods compact and walkable.

column3: Permanent bodily intervention does not replace the remainder of a sentence. Offenders receiving such punishment also serve substantially longer and more restrictive compulsory-service sentences and may remain subject to continuing restrictions afterward.
column4: Solarathi law distinguishes immediate restriction of future harm from the separate obligation to answer for harm already caused.

column3: Outside major cities, one noble administration may oversee several smaller towns and their surrounding countryside rather than every settlement having its own noble.
column4: The system favors practical administration rather than creating a noble office for every small settlement.

column3: Outside major cities, one noble family or administration may oversee several smaller towns and their surrounding countryside rather than every settlement having its own noble.
column4: The system favors practical administration over assigning aristocratic offices to every small settlement.

column3: Balconies and terraces are common on upper stories and provide space for outdoor living, plants, household work, cooking, and drying.
column4: Outdoor domestic life remains visible throughout Aldeatus's residential neighborhoods.

column3: Households without extensive private plumbing collect water from neighborhood fountains in clay vessels and carry it home.
column4: Fetching water is an ordinary part of neighborhood life.

column3: Marriage is understood as a genuine magical and sacred binding of two people's Heart Flames. Because of the seriousness of that bond, people are generally careful about choosing whom they bind themselves to.
column4: Marriage is not expected to be entered casually. The reality of the magical bond contributes to divorce being relatively uncommon without making divorce forbidden.

column3: People serving the most serious compulsory-service sentences live in guarded service residences. They receive food, clothing, shelter, medical care, and necessities but cannot earn ordinary wages and have substantially restricted movement.
column4: Even severe punishment generally favors controlled productive service over years spent inactive in a dungeon.

column3: Aldeatus's docks connect directly to major roads so goods arriving by lake and river can be transferred efficiently onto carts and wagons. Smaller routes carry goods onward into commercial and residential areas.
column4: The waterfront functions as one of the capital's major commercial gateways.

column3: Permanent stone or ceramic seats sit above wastewater channels. Flowing water carries waste into the sewer system, using gravity wherever possible.
column4: Cleanliness is culturally important.

column3: If both parents die or become unable to care for a child, the child's Radiant Guardians are the first expected alternative caregivers. A child may have one Avelum and one Solaver, and their lifelong oath includes responsibility for the child's guidance, protection, and well-being. If neither appropriate Radiant Guardian can take the child, suitable relatives are considered next. If no Guardian or relative can provide care, the child becomes a ward of the state.
column4: The system deliberately gives a child established trusted adults beyond their parents before relying upon institutional or state care. Radiant Guardians supplement family during ordinary life and become particularly important when parents are lost.

column3: Divorce exists but is relatively uncommon. Either spouse may initiate the process, but under ordinary circumstances both ultimately agree to dissolve the Flame Binding. A formal ceremony magically and religiously separates the previous union.
column4: People commonly describe dissolution as feeling as though they have genuinely lost part of themselves, so ending a Binding is treated seriously without being prohibited.

column3: Soldiers and knights currently have authority to intervene in serious disturbances and arrest people accused of crimes.
column4: Communities handle many minor problems informally, while serious matters enter the formal legal system.

column3: For ordinary crimes, the judicial band is removed completely once restitution or compulsory service has been completed.
column4: Solarath recognizes that a completed sentence is actually completed. Ordinary offenders are not permanently branded by wrongdoing after satisfying the judgment imposed upon them.

column3: Water is kept immediately beside fireplaces, stoves, and outdoor cooking fires so small fires can be extinguished before spreading. Sand, heavy cloth, lids, and other appropriate materials may also be used.
column4: Preventing one's household fire from threatening neighbors is considered a responsibility to the wider community.

column3: Small sellers and temporary stalls gather around neighborhood greens/squares alongside permanent neighborhood shops, allowing residents to obtain ordinary necessities without traveling to the main market.
column4: Sellers determine schedules according to their trade and customers. Businesses normally close for the midday meal.

column3: Skilled craftspeople producing individual goods are commonly paid per completed piece. A stained-glass artist commissioned to spend several cycles making a palace window, for example, receives the agreed payment when the completed work is delivered and accepted.
column4: The value of skilled work is tied to the finished object and expertise involved rather than simply the number of cycles spent producing it.

column3: Materials that were once alive retain an affinity for magic because they once carried a Heart Flame. Wood, bone, antler, and potentially other organic materials can be infused and used as magical reservoirs.
column4: Reusing animal and plant materials fits Solarath's broader resource ethic.

column3: Children whose manifested abilities qualify as body-related magic may explore Keeper training during the normal apprenticeship exploration period. Those who choose it follow the same broad age structure as other professions, but their training includes medicine, magical practice, and temple responsibilities.
column4: Keepers are not exempt from the normal expectation of long professional training simply because they possess useful magic.

column3: Adults can change professions later. Previous training determines how much entirely new knowledge they need; someone with existing business, customer, tool, or production experience may adapt more easily than a completely untrained person.
column4: Choosing a profession around age twelve establishes a first professional path, not an irreversible life assignment.

column3: Herbalists specialize in growing, identifying, preparing, preserving, and supplying medicinal plants and related ingredients.
column4: Herbalism is a skilled profession rather than merely gathering whatever plants happen to grow nearby.

column3: Public carriage services are supported through government revenue, including business taxes, trade tariffs, and Crown contributions. Drivers may be directly employed by the responsible administration or work under public contract. Rider fares may supplement this funding.
column4: Revenue generated by Aldeatus's economy helps maintain infrastructure used throughout the city.

column3: Wealthy households may contract directly with preferred producers and merchants for regular goods while continuing to purchase through ordinary markets, often through household staff.
column4: Markets remain points at which goods cross social boundaries.

column3: White and cream are the most common exterior colors, with pale/light pink, green, blue, yellow, purple, and orange also common. Red is not a normal exterior plaster color.
column4: The palette creates a bright cityscape when Aldeatus is viewed across the Great Lake.

column3: Some sensing abilities can amplify or share bodily sensations or signals with another person. A practitioner might allow another medical provider to hear or feel a patient's heartbeat, perceive blood flow, or feel fetal movement.
column4: Sharing allows several practitioners to examine the same otherwise invisible bodily process and has helped transform individual magical observations into teachable medical knowledge.

column3: Noble titles follow governmental succession rules separately from ordinary inheritance of wealth and property. Someone can legally inherit family property while being passed over as successor to a noble title if considered unsuitable for the administrative role.
column4: Solarath distinguishes owning something from being entrusted with authority over other people.

column3: At approximately age 20, after roughly eight Solturns of formal apprenticeship, the individual is considered fully trained in their profession. This generally coincides with Solarathi legal adulthood.
column4: Professional qualification and legal adulthood commonly occur around the same period of life.

column3: Tax money collected within a noble's territory is not necessarily spent only there. Aldeatus's administrations can redistribute funds between districts according to need.
column4: Residents are understood as part of Aldeatus and Solarath rather than only taxpayers of an isolated neighborhood. Public revenue therefore follows need as well as origin.

column3: Tax money collected within a noble's territory is not necessarily spent only there. Aldeatus's administrations can redistribute funds between districts according to need.
column4: Residents are understood as members of Aldeatus and Solarath rather than only taxpayers of an isolated district, so public resources can follow need as well as origin.

column3: If sufficient concern remains at review, the muted judicial band and relevant restrictions continue until the next review.
column4: Continued identification is periodically justified rather than assumed forever, except where the Royal Court explicitly imposed a permanent restriction.

column3: Glass windows occur across social classes. Many are designed to remain open during warmer weather and are protected by shutters when conditions become cold or severe.
column4: Open windows help connect houses with courtyards, streets, and neighborhood life.

column3: Job loss or temporary inability to earn is initially handled largely through family, friends, neighbors, and community resources while the person regains stability. State assistance can supplement local support when the need exceeds what the community can reasonably provide.
column4: Community support is partly preventative: keeping someone fed, housed, and connected reduces desperation while reinforcing mutual responsibility.

column3: At twenty, a person is legally an adult and may freely choose to marry. At eighteen or nineteen, marriage requires both parental permission and court permission. People under eighteen cannot legally marry.
column4: Marriage law treats adulthood and ability to independently consent as more important than family status or sex.

column3: A large general market fills the main city square approximately once per span. Farmers, ranchers, craftspeople, merchants, and other sellers bring larger selections than are ordinarily available through neighborhood shops.
column4: The market is both commercial and social.

column3: Starting schools operate 6 cycles per span. Classes begin shortly after first light and end around midday. Because daylight changes through the Solturn, a school cycle generally lasts approximately 4–6 hours.
column4: The schedule intentionally leaves children substantial time for family life, neighborhood responsibilities, play, and practical learning.

column3: Unless the deceased specifies otherwise, ordinary inheritance passes first to the surviving spouse. If there is no surviving spouse, it passes to the oldest child. A person can establish different wishes beforehand. The inheritor controls the inherited property and decides whether to distribute portions among siblings or other relatives.
column4: Equality of Heart Flames does not mean every material resource must be divided equally. Solarathi inheritance law recognizes individual property ownership even when that can create inequality.

column3: Long-term employees are generally paid on a recurring schedule, such as twice per month or monthly. Exact arrangements depend upon employer and profession.
column4: There is no expectation that every profession uses an identical pay schedule.

column3: Communal fountains are distributed throughout residential areas, particularly around neighborhood greens and gathering spaces. Many are wall fountains with one or more continuously flowing spouts and stone basins. Larger public spaces may have more elaborate tiered fountains. Residents fill clay vessels directly from them for household water.
column4: Fountains function as both necessary infrastructure and everyday gathering places.

column3: Serious injuries, dangerous illness, difficult births, and other unstable conditions may require temple care because multiple trained people, supplies, continuous observation, and specialized magic are available there.
column4: Moving someone to a temple indicates that their condition requires resources beyond ordinary home care.

column3: Certain severe offenders may leave compulsory service wearing a muted cream, tan, or undyed version of their offense-pattern judicial band rather than having the band removed. This identifies a completed sentence accompanied by continuing public-safety restrictions.
column4: The muted band distinguishes someone no longer undergoing active punishment from someone whose past offense still creates legally recognized safety concerns.

column3: Major holidays and festivals can bring larger specialty markets featuring foreign and regional foods, spices, textiles, crafts, and unusual goods.
column4: Specialty markets contribute to major celebrations and expose residents to cultures from elsewhere in Avelis.

column3: Solarath has no universal equivalent to a weekend. How many cycles someone works during a span depends upon profession, household finances, workload, season, and personal need.
column4: Working fewer cycles is not inherently regarded as laziness if the household's needs are comfortably met and responsibilities are fulfilled.

column3: Only materials that have exhausted reasonable reuse options are burned: ruined plant-fiber textiles, unusable wood remnants, ruined paper/parchment, contaminated organics, diseased vegetation, certain medical/birthing waste, dead vermin, spoiled animal matter, and similar materials. Useful wood is retained as fuel/material.
column4: Burning is a final stage of use and may be understood as returning the material to the Flame.

column3: Certain metals can draw stored magic from an infused reservoir and conduct it into another object or system.

The palace employs large numbers of Aldeatus residents for domestic, administrative, craft, maintenance, stable, guard, food, garden, and other work. Some employees already live in Aldeatus; others relocate to the capital after obtaining palace employment.
column4: The palace functions simultaneously as a royal residence, seat of government, and major economic institution within Aldeatus.

column3: Post-sentence identification can accompany continuing restrictions regarding access to children, particular occupations, residences, or situations relevant to the original offense.
column4: Completion of compulsory labor does not automatically restore privileges the court has determined could create continuing danger.

column3: Businesses determine their hours according to trade and customers. Some operate primarily during daylight while others remain open into the night.
column4: Aldeatus remains active at different hours rather than universally opening and closing together.

column3: Someone unable to repay substantial restitution may perform labor whose assessed value is credited toward the amount owed rather than receiving ordinary wages until the debt is satisfied.
column4: Labor represents repayment of a specific harm rather than ownership of the offender's labor by the harmed person.

column3: People under continuing post-sentence identification attend counseling approximately once or twice each Solturn. Sessions examine behavior, accountability, rehabilitation, current concerns, and adjustment following the sentence.
column4: Counseling is intended both to support rehabilitation and to provide information relevant to continued restrictions.

column3: If reviewers determine that continuing identification and associated restrictions are no longer necessary, they can recommend removal of the muted judicial band and restoration of the relevant legal privileges.
column4: Removal represents genuine legal restoration based upon demonstrated change rather than merely the passage of a predetermined amount of time.

column3: Counseling occurs before and after dissolution of a Flame Binding. It helps determine whether dissolution is genuinely desired and supports the former spouses through the emotional and spiritual consequences afterward.
column4: Because Flame Binding creates a real connection, post-dissolution distress is expected and treated as worthy of care rather than evidence that divorce itself was necessarily a mistake.

column3: Each moon, business income is considered against legitimate costs such as stock and materials, employee wages, and reasonable support for the owner's household. A percentage of what remains is owed to the Crown.
column4: The system is intended to avoid taxing a struggling shop into failure merely because substantial money passed through the business.

column3: Particularly serious cases, cases involving major consequences, and matters referred upward by the public court are decided by the monarch and Royal Court.
column4: The Crown functions as Solarath's highest judicial authority, while ordinary disputes remain decentralized.

column3: Local councils represent communities beneath noble administrations and participate in major decisions concerning those administrations, including matters related to appointment or removal of nobles.
column4: Local councils provide the lower level of the same decentralized system in which matters should be handled as close to the affected population as practical.

column3: At yearly or twice-yearly intervals, continuing restrictions and identification are formally reconsidered using information from counseling and the person's conduct since the previous review.
column4: A severe conviction does not automatically mean permanent public identification. Continued restriction must remain subject to reassessment unless the original judgment explicitly made a particular restriction permanent.

column2: In smaller towns, children commonly learn trades locally, often through family businesses or established local craftspeople. Training continues into young adulthood, generally through about age 20.
column3: Depends on trade; relevant magic is incorporated into practical training where useful.

Around age 20, trained young adults may choose to travel to a larger city for roughly 2–4 additional years of deeper or specialized education in their trade. This is optional rather than necessary for ordinary employment.
column4: City training is viewed as specialization rather than the only route to being considered properly trained.

column3: After local or advanced training, people may begin working locally, remain in the city where they specialized, return to their home community, or move to another town/city where their skills are needed.
column4: Creates natural movement of skilled workers between settlements while still allowing strong multigenerational local businesses.

column3: In smaller communities, remaining in the same family profession or business is especially common because children grow up around the work and can enter an already functioning operation rather than building one from the ground up.
column4: Family continuity is common through convenience and familiarity, not social obligation. Changing professions is normal and permitted.

column3: The world of Avelis, regarded in Solarathi belief as the eternal vessel that receives and sustains all life.
column4: Avelis is honored alongside the Eternal Flame. Together, earth and sun represent the beginning and end of all life.

column3: The eastern continent, home to Solareth, the Western Kingdom, and the dwarven kingdom of the Kharum Range.
column4: Its kingdoms possess distinct cultures, histories, and traditions.

column3: The largest kingdom of Eldren, with its capital at Aldeatus.
column4: Solarathi society is deeply influenced by devotion to the Eternal Flame. Its monarch is traditionally a bearer of solar power.

column3: The western continent, home to Halabe, Ranery, Vestele, and territories and vassal states associated with Solareth.
column4: Fryke lies across the waters from Eldren.

column3: The capital city of Solareth, situated beside the Great Lake and sheltered by the Solareth Mountains. It serves as the political and cultural heart of the kingdom.
column4: Aldeatus shares its name with the ruling royal family, House Aldeatus, reflecting the close association between the city and the Solarathi monarchy.
