column3: The sacred city of Solareth, nestled within a volcanic mountain basin.
column4: Pilgrims travel here to honor the Eternal Flame. Its glassmakers produce some of the most prized stained glass in Avelis.

column3: A volcanic mountain range forming Solareth's northwestern border and home to the dwarven kingdom.
column4: The mountains form an important geographical boundary between neighboring peoples.

column3: A volcanic mountain range surrounding the sacred basin of Veshalor.
column4: Considered among the holiest landscapes in Avelis.

column3: The first light and source of all life, understood as the sun itself.
column4: Believed to know, give, and sustain all. Every Heart Flame originates from the Eternal Flame and eventually returns to it.

column3: A living fragment of the Eternal Flame carried by every mortal.
column4: Caring for one's Heart Flame through choices and deeds is considered a fundamental responsibility.

column3: A divine servant of the Eternal Flame, entrusted with guiding and protecting the world.
column4: The Radiants are honored collectively through prayer, festivals, and daily devotion rather than worshipped individually.

column3: A sworn member of the Order of Aurelis, devoted to the temples and the Radiants.
column4: Following their vows, members place Aurelis before their birth family name, symbolizing their adoption into the order while honoring their lineage.

column3: A sworn member of the Order of Embryn, responsible for guarding sacred flames and those under their protection.
column4: Members place Embryn before their birth family name upon completing their sacred vows.

column3: Any living being entrusted with a Heart Flame, including people, animals, and plants.
column4: Solarathi belief teaches that all living things carry sacred life, while humanity possesses the freedom to choose how to honor that gift.

column3: The sacred union of two mortals before the Eternal Flame, joining their lives and allowing their magic to answer as one.
column4: Following the ceremony, the couple returns home to their Binding Baskets and spends one span together celebrating their union.

column3: A sacred rite within Flame Binding in which the couple's hands are joined by a woven cord.
column4: The cord contains three strands: one for each partner and a golden strand representing the Eternal Flame. Their magic is joined while each retains their individual Heart Flame.

column3: A woven basket prepared for a newly bound couple and filled with gifts for their shared life.
column4: The eldest bound couple attending each weave a basket. Family and friends fill them with bread, honey, herbs, fruit, keepsakes, and other offerings.

column3: Small bells worn around the waist or abdomen during pregnancy.
column4: Their sound is believed to guide a child's Heart Flame to its mother. After birth, bells may be incorporated into Parental Bands to preserve the familiar sound.

column3: Bands worn around the thigh or calf, with one band representing each child.
column4: The bands are arranged from top to bottom in order of birth.

column3: A sworn protector entrusted with the lifelong guidance and well-being of a child.
column4: A Solarathi child may have one Avelum and one Solaver, whose oaths are made to the child, family, and Radiants.

column3: A woman sworn to serve as a Radiant Guardian.
column4: Provides counsel, protection, and care whenever called upon by the child or family.

column3: A man sworn to serve as a Radiant Guardian.
column4: Provides counsel, protection, and care whenever called upon by the child or family.

column3: Matched upper-arm bands representing the significant bonds of a person's life
column4: The first cuff is received at Coming of Age and worn on the right arm, engraved with the wearer's name. A second is received at Flame Binding and worn on the left, engraved with the partner's name. Materials vary according to personal means.

column3: A gold collar worn by members of the Solarathi royal family.
column4: The band represents both royal honor and responsibility. Individual designs may include engravings or gemstones, and bands may occasionally be bestowed upon favored individuals outside the royal family.

column3: The period between one sunrise and the next.
column4: Each new cycle represents another opportunity to grow, serve, and honor the Eternal Flame.

column3: A period consisting of ten cycles.
column4: Households commonly organize work, travel, and celebrations around spans.

column3: A division of the Solturn consisting of four spans, or forty cycles.
column4: Festivals, harvests, and community gatherings are often associated with particular moons.

column3: One complete journey of Avelis around the Eternal Flame, consisting of ten moons, forty spans, or four hundred cycles.
column4: The passing of a Solturn is celebrated with gratitude for another year beneath the Eternal Flame.
